Then the left wing of the Franks attacked
the right wing of the Arabs (Muslims),
in which was Taqi al-Din Umar, the nephew of Saladin;
and he held out firmly before the Franks.
And when the king of the Franks saw that the Arabs did not waver,
he took courage in his spirit,
and signed the cross upon his face,
and charged against the center, that is, the heart of the forces of the Arabs,
in which were al-Afdal and Zafir, the sons of Saladin,
and Qutb al-Din, son of Nur al-Din, son of Qara Arslan, the lord of Hisn Kayfa,
and Ibn Lashin (or: Lajin?), the lord of Nablus,
and many others.
And when they joined battle with one another,
the Franks were cutting down the Arabs as if with scythes.
And the Arabs began to flee,
and the Franks were after them with swords and horns sounding mightily;
and there was a great defeat among the Arabs.
And the Franks reached the camp of the Arabs,
and looted the tents,
and killed all the merchants.
And the fugitives of the Arabs reached as far as Damascus and Tiberias.
And the Franks, having pursued the Arabs for about a parasang, turned back;
and they saw that the left wing of the Arabs had not moved from its position.
And because they were weary,
while those were fresh (resting),
they did not engage with them,
but went and encamped in their tents.
Saladin, however, by shouts, cries, and encouragements, turned back the fugitives;
and they came and settled in their tents like dead men.
And the slain who fell were numbered at four thousand and one hundred,
because Saladin ordered the Arabs who were inside Acre,
and they went out and cast them into the sea.
And a man stood with a cord in his hand,
and whenever they threw in a corpse,
he tied a knot.
And of the Franks there fell about two thousand.
Then the nobles advised Saladin to depart from that place
and withdraw a little from the Franks.
And they made an excuse,
saying, 'A corruption of the air has occurred in this meadow from the stench of the slain.'
And when the Arabs departed and encamped in a distant place,
the Franks dug a great trench from the hill to the sea between themselves and the force of the Arabs that was outside,
and they surrounded Acre from sea to sea.
